articles.title: Coinbase and State Department Host Dublin DPRK Crypto Symposium
articles.summary: Coinbase and the US State Department co-sponsored a two-day Dublin symposium on North Korean cyber threats to crypto, joined by Global Affairs Canada, Google, and Payward. FBI, FinCEN, and Ireland's Garda National Cyber Crime Bureau participated in sessions covering two DPRK threat vectors: crypto heists funneling proceeds into weapons programs and fake IT workers using false identities to secure remote positions at crypto firms. The event consolidates US, Canadian, and Irish law enforcement with major crypto and tech companies into a shared operational framework for countering state-sponsored financial crime.

articles.title: Push to scrap SEC's Regulation Crypto and innovation exemption
articles.summary: Senators Warren, Van Hollen, and Tina Smith, with other Banking Committee members, sent SEC Chair Atkins two letters demanding the agency withdraw its crypto offering rules and its tokenized stock "innovation exemption." The August proposal exempts crypto offerings up to $5M for four years and up to $75M for one year from registration. The five-year innovation exemption would keep tokenized securities venues from being treated as exchanges, which the senators say creates a "shadow stock market" that fragments liquidity and invites illicit finance.

articles.title: OKXICE Opens 24/7 Stock Trading With Six Live Tokens
articles.summary: OKX launched OKXICE, a tokenized stock trading platform routing six equity tokens through Uniswap v4 pools for 24/7 on-chain trading. The inaugural pools held $1.22 million in liquidity after the first day, and OKX has confirmed a rollout pipeline of 113 total assets including the current listings. The Uniswap v4 integration makes these tokens composable with existing DeFi protocols, extending tokenized equities beyond isolated wrappers into natively on-chain instruments.

articles.title: Backpack Launches Open RFQ Marketplace for Stock Order Flow
articles.summary: Backpack Exchange launched an RFQ system for stocks, letting any market maker submit two-sided quotes that compete with Backpack's own executing broker on each order. The system combines native Backpack liquidity with traditional finance liquidity, routing retail stock orders to whichever counterparty offers the best price at execution time. Open access means any market maker can plug in without special arrangements, increasing competitive pressure on each fill across Backpack's stock order flow. The design mirrors RFQ mechanisms common in traditional equity markets, where fragmented liquidity pools compete on price rather than posting to a single central order book.

articles.title: 2026 Onchain AI Portfolio Review and 2027 Reallocation Plans
articles.summary: 0xJeff, a prominent Onchain AI sector investor, published a 2026 portfolio retrospective acknowledging mixed results across the year and sharing specific holdings, mistakes, and lessons. 2026 was a difficult period for Onchain AI token allocations, consistent with broader crypto market pressure following BTC's decline from October 2025 highs. There will be 2027 reallocation plans within the Onchain AI sector, indicating a repositioning rather than an exit from the category.

articles.title: 75+ Free Tier Crypto APIs Cataloged Across 10 Categories
articles.summary: A developer-compiled directory at freecryptoapis.com catalogs 75+ free-tier access points across 10 categories, from swap aggregators to security tooling, giving builders a single reference for assembling zero-cost infrastructure stacks. The most generous allocations include dRPC at 50M compute units/month, Helius at 1M credits/month, Alchemy at 30M compute units/month, 1inch at 100K calls/month, and Neynar at 10M credits/month. A dozen entries require no API key at all, including Jupiter, DEX Screener, Hyperliquid, Binance, PublicNode across 77 chains, Pyth, ENS, and mempool.space. Category coverage runs deepest in RPC/node providers (12), market data (12), and swap/execution (11), with explorers (8), analytics/indexing (7), identity/social (6), and oracles (5) rounding out the set.

articles.title: Aave vs Morpho: An Asset Issuer's Guide
articles.summary: Aave V4 pools liquidity in Hubs that Spokes borrow from up to a cap, so unrecovered debt becomes a Hub deficit shared by all suppliers of that asset, while Morpho's isolated markets with five fixed parameters keep bad debt inside one market and the curator vault that funded it. Morpho holds about $11.3B in deposits against $15.8B on Aave V3, and during April's Kelp rsETH exploit, Aave lost $8.45B in deposits over 48 hours while Morpho's losses stayed in rsETH-exposed markets. Morpho's liquidation formula gives a 62.5% LLTV market such as Robinhood's NVDA a 12.7% incentive and 2.7x theoretical leverage, versus 2.6% and 11.8x at 91.5% LLTV. Recommended venues by asset: Morpho first for yield-bearing stablecoins with Aave for scale, wherever borrowers are for payment stablecoins, Horizon for credit RWAs, and the distribution partner's venue for tokenized stocks, such as Coinbase's Aave V4 Spoke and Robinhood's Morpho markets.

articles.title: How to market tokenized assets
articles.summary: RWA products are good, but few people outside crypto know about them because marketing speaks to crypto insiders. Lead with the problem rather than the technology, explain what being onchain adds, and market beyond Crypto Twitter through YouTube, TikTok, finance podcasts, and creators. Partnering with fintechs, neobanks, and brokers that already have users lets the blockchain stay invisible. Content should explain where yield comes from, what backs the asset, who is responsible, and what the risks are, since trust is part of the product. Tokenization is early, like cards or Apple Pay once were.

articles.title: Nvidia agrees to $290 million settlement over crypto mining disclosures
articles.summary: Nvidia will pay $290M to settle a class action alleging it understated crypto mining's contribution to 2017 and 2018 gaming GPU sales.
